shopify.text: Native. The checkout editor (colours, fonts, logo, corners, layout) is available on every plan; only the Checkout Branding API and apps that customise the information, shipping and payment pages are Plus.

Rated partial on re-reading the code (first report: full, not rechecked).
criteria: Stripe's payment form takes its primary colour, text colours, font family and corner radius from the store's theme, in the light and the dark set (a unit test of the appearance function for two themes).

shopify.text: Native. Manual capture is on every plan; cards must be captured within the authorisation period (7 days with Shopify Payments, a longer period for Plus, with a fee after 7 days).

criteria: A store can switch to manual capture; a paid session then leaves the order authorised, not paid, with the stock held.
Staff capture the amount (or less) from the order page before the authorisation expires; the order then becomes paid and counts in sales.
An authorisation that expires or is voided releases the stock and cancels the order.
Analytics and refunds treat an uncaptured payment as not paid.

history.why: Wave 4 unit B (D289): an owner chooses when the card is charged (at checkout, when sent, when staff capture); a store that waits opens its checkout sessions with capture_method manual for goods (never subscriptions, bookings, deposits, hosts' listings or downloads), and a paid session leaves the order authorized with its stock held to a day past the hold's end. Staff capture the whole or less from the order page (the rest released as a release refund with its credit note), or the first parcel or handover captures it; the order then becomes paid through complete_order_payment() and counts from then. Cancel and release, Stripe's payment_intent.canceled and the job past the deadline (a staff email a day before) cancel the order and release its stock. Analytics' paid order needs a captured payment, so a held card counts nowhere. Held by payment-capture.int.test.ts (hold, capture, less than held with a credit note, euro, when sent, by hand refused at sending, void, Stripe's cancel, warning and expiry), src/db/capture.test.ts and the signed-in browser test.

shopify.text: Native. Shopify Payments runs fraud analysis on every order and flags medium and high risk with a warning on the Orders list.

criteria: A paid order shows Stripe's risk outcome (normal, elevated, highest) read from the charge, in the order list and on the order page.
Staff filter orders by risk and can hold fulfilment on an elevated one.
The risk shown is only what Stripe reported; none is invented when Stripe gave none.
A flagged order that is refunded or disputed is visible as such.

history.why: Wave 4 unit A (D288): Stripe's risk outcome (level and score) is read from the charge and kept on the payment; the order page's Payment card shows Stripe: elevated or highest risk with the score, the list shows a risk badge and filters by it (pay=elevated_risk), and an automation rule can hold an order by Stripe's risk (condition risk, never met while the charge is unread). Nothing is shown for normal or not assessed and nothing is invented. A disputed order carries its Disputed badge beside the risk; a refunded one its payment state. Held by payment-disputes.int.test.ts, order-rules.test.ts, payment-card.test.ts and the signed-in browser test. Radar's own review queue stays in the store's Stripe Dashboard.

shopify.text: Native. Chargebacks under Shopify Payments are managed in the admin (evidence-submission window; the amount is taken from the next payout, plus the bank's fee).

criteria: A dispute opened in Stripe appears on the order with its amount, reason and the evidence deadline.
Staff are emailed once when a dispute opens and again before the deadline.
A lost dispute is recorded as money out in the order and the finance analytics, once; a won one clears the flag.
A refund made in the Stripe Dashboard is recorded on the order through the same webhook (idempotent).

history.why: Wave 4 unit A (D288): the connected account's charge.dispute.* events are kept as commerce.payment_disputes (one row per dispute, identity fixed, a closed dispute kept as it closed, never deleted); the order page shows the amount, reason, status and evidence deadline in the store's time zone with a link to the dispute in the store's Stripe Dashboard, where evidence is sent; the order's history says when it opened and closed; staff are emailed once when it opens and once three days before the deadline (staff alert dispute); a lost dispute is money out in the Finance bridge, once, in the period it closed, without VAT plus the fee where known, never a refund or credit note; a won one clears the Disputed mark. A refund made in Stripe's Dashboard was already recorded through the same webhook (D159, invoice-refunds.int.test.ts). Held by payment-disputes.int.test.ts (replayed events, a lost dispute, a reminder once, an unknown payment, euro), src/db/payment-facts.test.ts and the signed-in browser test.

Amounts convert through the euro at the store's rates and round to the currency's step; a currency without a rate is not converted.

feature: EU VAT by destination, VAT-inclusive prices, reduced rates

shopify.text: Native. Shopify sets tax rates automatically (Shopify Tax, or manual settings; Basic Tax in the EU only for stores set up before 13 May 2026) and lets the merchant set tax overrides for products with special rates. Shopify does not remit or file tax. Tax-inclusive pricing is not described on the pages read.

gap: Unit 1a (D157 proposed, docs/wave-1a-tax.md) built criteria 1 to 4 and the audit half of 6: `commerce.vat_categories` (standard, exempt, accommodation, food, books, periodicals, medicines, culture_events, children_goods; the product's category is a foreign key), `commerce.vat_rates` with validity dates, source, checked-on date and a verified flag, written only by `commerce.set_vat_rate()` (a period ends, a new one begins, audit-logged) and read only through `commerce.vat_rate(country, category, at)` (`vat-readers.test.ts` scans the source), a per-country shipping VAT rule that only applies once a person has verified it, the product editor's category select, and the platform page `/admin/platform/vat`. Tests: `src/db/vat.test.ts`, `vat-admin.int.test.ts`, and `checkout-kinds.int.test.ts` (each category, a mixed basket, in the market's currency and in euro view, `cartSummary()` equal to `placeOrder()`, a rate change that leaves placed orders alone). Unit 1c (D161 proposed) built criterion 5 and the reconciliation half of criterion 6: the VAT report per country and rate for a period with refunds netted through credit notes, exported as CSV in the owner's period, and a bridge to Finance and to the sum of `tax_minor` of paid orders that names every difference and leaves out copied and host orders (`tax-reports.int.test.ts`, `src/db/tax-reports.test.ts`); unit 1b's invoice takes the line's rate (the snapshot's buckets, `checkout-kinds.int.test.ts`). Still missing: (1) the rate data is thin and unverified: besides the 28 standard rates only Norway, Sweden, Finland and Germany have reduced rows for food, books, periodicals and culture (13 reduced-rate rows in all, none for medicines or children's goods, plus three accommodation rows), every row is unverified (no person has checked it against TEDB or with an accountant; the TEDB was not readable), and a country with no row charges the standard rate, so a French or Spanish food product is taxed at the standard rate until a platform admin enters the rate; (2) every shipping VAT rule is the standard one, none verified; (3) the platform VAT page and the product editor's category select are now driven in a browser (e2e/signed-in/vat-screens.spec.ts, 2026-10-19: a platform admin schedules a rate, which starts unverified; an owner moves a product to Books and saves); (4) the catalogue's cached VAT label can lag a scheduled rate change by up to the cache lifetime between the country's midnight and the daily 07:00 UTC job. Stripe Tax is not used.
criteria: An owner puts a product in a reduced-rate category (food, books, children's goods, others) and the cart, order and invoice take that country's rate (a scenario in checkout-kinds.int.test.ts).
Platform admins edit categories and per-country rates in the admin, with history; a rate is only ever read through `commerce.vat_rate()`.
Shipping takes the rate the law requires for the goods, or the standard rate where stated.
Every seeded rate carries its source and the date it was checked.
A VAT report per country and rate for a period (net, VAT, gross, refunds netted) can be exported as CSV in the layout an OSS return needs; refunds and credit notes reduce it.

The report agrees with the sum of orders' `tax_minor` for the period (a test holds it) and leaves out copied and host orders; edits to categories and rates are audit-logged and apply to new carts and orders only.

shopify.text: Native. Merchants register their OSS credentials (EU-based) or IOSS number (outside the EU, consignments up to 150 euro) in tax settings and Shopify collects VAT by destination; OSS needs Shopify Tax or Basic Tax, and does not apply when the fulfilment location is outside the EU. Shopify does not file the return.

gap: Unit 1a (D157 proposed) records the registration and marks the order: `commerce.store_tax_profile` holds the VAT registration, the OSS scheme (Union with its member state, or non-Union with its EU number) and the IOSS number, intermediary, markets and date, with format checks, owners only, edited at `/admin/{store}/settings/tax`; checkout charges destination VAT on every consumer sale, and a consignment of at most 150 EUR sent from outside the EU to a private buyer in a listed market is marked `vat_kind = 'ioss'` with the IOSS number on the order, page and email; above 150.00 EUR, a business buyer, an unlisted market, a store sending from inside the EU, downloads and a currency with no euro rate are not marked. Unit 1b's invoice and credit note carry the IOSS statement and the number (D159, `treatment.iossNumber`, `order-document-view.test.ts`). Unit 1c (D161 proposed, `docs/wave-1c-reports.md`) built the return data: `/admin/{store}/analytics/tax?view=oss|ioss` gives the quarterly Union and non-Union and the monthly IOSS data per Member State of consumption and rate (Part 2 with the Member State of dispatch for 2b and 2d, Part 3 corrections, Part 4, Part 5) in euro at the ECB's reference rate of the period's last day (or the owner's audited override), from invoices and credit notes only, with a formula-safe CSV that is refused while a rate is missing, an export log with a drift line, deadlines, registration warnings and read-only AI tools; a refund reduces the period through its credit note (books mode in its own month, filing mode a Part 3 correction of the sale's period). Tests: `tax-reports.int.test.ts` (a worked example from real orders, IOSS with an above-150 order, a business buyer and a next-month credit), `oss-return.test.ts`, `tax-csv.test.ts`, `tax-report-admin.int.test.ts`, `oss-view.test.ts`. Still short of Full: (1) bucket B: live only with an OSS or IOSS registration the owner holds, and no number is checked against any register; (2) Kaizen files nothing: the data is what a return asks for in its boxes, for the owner's accountant, and which part of a return a sale belongs in (`classify()`, spec 4.3: goods dispatched from outside the EU that were not IOSS sales, booked services, business buyers charged VAT, fee lines, a Norwegian store using the Union scheme) has not been read by an accountant; (3) a refund of an order with no invoice (invoicing off, waiting, test mode) is in no return and shows only in the informational refunds line; (4) the OSS registration changes nothing in checkout (destination VAT was already the rule; the 10,000 EUR threshold and the origin-country rule are not applied, said on the screen); (5) neither the tax screen nor the report page was opened in a browser with data (render and action tests only, the admin needs a sign-in); (6) the IOSS statement and import notice are hand-written and unreviewed, and what counts as intrinsic value for the 150 EUR test is an open question for an accountant; (7) the EC Sales List and each state's own return mapping are not built (wave 2).
criteria: An owner enters an OSS or IOSS registration; checkout uses destination VAT as the registration requires.
A quarterly (OSS) and monthly (IOSS) report gives sales, VAT base and VAT by country and rate as a CSV export holding the data a return asks for in its boxes (Kaizen files nothing).
A consignment of 150 euro or less from outside the EU is charged destination VAT at checkout and marked IOSS on the order and invoice.
A refund reduces the period's VAT in the report through its credit note (a refund of an order with no invoice appears only in the refunds line).

history.why: Unit 1a (docs/wave-1a-tax.md): read the code and ran tax-profile, ioss, vat-engine and vat-money-review tests: the OSS and IOSS registration is stored with format and market rules, and an order of at most 150 EUR from outside the EU is marked IOSS in the running cart and order (150.00 yes, 150.01 no, no euro rate no). Kept partial and not Full: the OSS and IOSS reports (1c) and the invoice marking (1b) do not exist, and bucket B needs a registration the owner holds.

feature: B2B VAT ID, reverse charge, exemption

shopify.text: Native, with conditions. Since February 2026 checkout can validate a company VAT number and apply the reverse charge for EU to EU and EU to UK orders; it needs Shopify Tax in the EU or UK and an EU fulfilment location, and the Company VAT number field set to optional.

gap: Unit 1a (D157 proposed) built the checkout side: a business in another EU country enters its VAT number in the cart's `cart_checkout` piece, `src/server/vies.ts` checks it (one constant host, an injectable fetch, 4 s, one retry, a 24-hour cache in `commerce.vat_checks`, limits taken atomically), and `vatTreatment()` (pure, one reason code per refusal) decides; a valid number for the delivery country takes the VAT off (`orders.vat_kind = 'reverse_charge'`, the VAT not charged is `vat_relief_minor` inside the discount, the total is exactly the old total minus the old tax), the check, number and time are kept on the order, Stripe is sent the net amounts, and the order page, the confirmation email and the staff order page say 'Reverse charge' with both numbers in nb, sv, da and en. A VIES failure, a stale check, an invalid number, a consumer, the seller's own country, a seller number not checked valid, a booking, a subscription, a host's listing, goods sent from outside the EU or from the delivery country all charge VAT with the reason said. Tests: `vat-treatment.test.ts` (matrix), `vat-engine.int.test.ts` (cart equals order, Stripe lines equal the amount due, euro and koruna views, with a code, a campaign, a group discount and credits), `vies.test.ts`, `vat-security.int.test.ts`, `e2e/vat-reverse-charge.spec.ts` (valid takes the VAT off, a 503 charges VAT, own country shows no field). Still missing: (1) the invoice and credit note carry the reverse-charge statement and both numbers (D159: `order-document-view.test.ts`, `invoice-snapshot.test.ts`, `invoice-issue.int.test.ts`, `invoice-refunds.int.test.ts`); the wording is hand-written and unreviewed; (2) VIES was never called live: every test uses an injected fetch or the stub server, so the live service's answers are known only from its published specification read on 2026-10-03; (3) the e2e does not press Checkout (a test database has no Stripe), the payment step is held by the integration tests against a fake Stripe; (4) the store's tax screen is now driven in a browser (e2e/signed-in/vat-screens.spec.ts, 2026-10-19: registered, a Swedish number refused for a Norwegian store, a Norwegian one saved); (5) the reverse-charge wording and the VAT-number texts are hand-written and unreviewed (legal review), and open questions remain for an accountant (credits used at their VAT-inclusive value, downloads sold to a business in another member state, a per-location dispatch country); (6) a Norwegian store cannot use reverse charge and a non-EU buyer's number is never accepted (stated limits); (7) the exemption is given automatically on a valid registration: a buyer counts as a business when it types a company name and an organisation number, and VIES says only that the number is registered, not whose it is, so a private buyer who types any company and a third party's public VAT number gets the VAT taken off; the staff order page flags a VIES name that differs from the typed company, but only after the order, and nothing in code compares them; (8) the VIES limits bound the harm and do not remove it: a visitor with several addresses can spend the store's 60 requests an hour for shoppers (a client is held to 20, a cart to 10), after which real business buyers see 'could not be checked' and are charged VAT until the hour turns (said in docs/wave-1a-tax.md section 3.5).
criteria: A business shopper enters an EU VAT number at checkout; it is checked against VIES, and a valid one for another member state takes the VAT off the order.
The number, the check's result and its time are kept on the order; an unavailable VIES service never blocks the sale and never silently exempts it.
The invoice and order email say 'reverse charge' with both numbers.
Exemption never applies to consumers or to the seller's own country.

history.why: Unit 1a (docs/wave-1a-tax.md): read the code and ran vat-treatment, vies, vat-engine, vat-security and vat-money-review tests and e2e/vat-reverse-charge.spec.ts against the final tree: a valid VIES number for the delivery country takes the VAT off the cart and the order, the check is kept on the order, a VIES failure charges VAT and never blocks, order page and email say Reverse charge with both numbers. Kept partial: Kaizen's own invoice (1b) does not exist, VIES was never called live, and the legal wording is unreviewed.

shopify.text: Native on Basic, Grow and Advanced (payment terms moved from Plus to all plans); partial payments and deposits stay Plus.

gap: Built (D293): a company has payment terms (15, 30 or 60 days) and an optional credit limit; its accounts choose Pay by invoice at checkout, the order is confirmed with nothing paid, its stock drawn and its invoice issued with the due date; reminders go three days before and the day after, staff get an overdue alert, the control center and Finance show what is due and overdue, and the order is paid from its page on Stripe's hosted page or recorded as paid outside. Left: a paid order is dated by the day it was placed, as every order in Kaizena Flow's figures is, not the day it was paid (criterion 3); a balance cannot be paid in part; a store on Mollie alone has no Pay now; no browser test of the checkout choice yet.
criteria: A company account has payment terms (net 15, 30, 60); its checkout places the order unpaid with a due date and holds stock.
Staff or the customer see the due date; a reminder goes before it and an overdue mark after.
Marking it paid, or paying by a link, makes the order paid and counts it in sales on that day.
An overdue order shows in the control center and the analytics.

history.why: Payment terms for company accounts (D293): placed unpaid with a due date and its invoice, reminded, overdue in the control center and Finance, paid by a link or recorded, in tests. Sales are dated by the order day, not the payment day.

shopify.text: Native. Abandoned checkout emails with a recovery link and optional discount.

gap: Evidence debt: the erasure after 60 days (`KEEP_DAYS` in `sendDueCartReminders()`) and the admin figures from `cartReminderStats()` are in the code but no listed test asserts them.
criteria: With reminders on, a typed email captures the cart, and up to three reminders go at the owner's delays, each with its own optional code, words per language and a button that restores the cart.
At most one reminder per cart per run, none after the cart is paid, the same email buys, or the shopper opts out; each is claimed before it is sent.
Every email has a one-click unsubscribe (List-Unsubscribe headers) and the data is erased on opt-out and after 60 days.
The admin shows carts captured, reminded and recovered, with the sales.

shopify.text: Native. Monetary, percentage, buy X get Y and free-shipping discounts, as codes or automatic; combinations and eligibility are set per discount.

gap: Both mechanisms work: codes (percent, fixed amount per market, free shipping, minimum order and minimum number of items, dates, total and per-customer limits, recurring; products, categories and tags; customer groups or named customers; generated single-use codes with a CSV, D299 E1) and automatic campaigns (D114 to D116: percentage, buy N pay M, free product, categories and tags, customer groups, stacking). Still one code per order with no combination choices (D299 E2), no automatic amount off or free shipping (E3) and no buy X get Y (E4).
criteria: A code can be limited to categories and tags, to a customer group or named customers, and to a minimum quantity.
A store generates a batch of unique codes and exports them.
An owner chooses which discounts combine; the cart and `placeOrder()` agree on the result.
Every new kind has scenarios in checkout-kinds.int.test.ts, one of them in euro.

history.why: Re-read at HEAD: codes reach products only (`discount_codes.product_ids`), one code per order, no customer eligibility or bulk generation; the Customers domain rates the same two features partial.

shopify.text: Native. Cancel an order, refund in full or in part to the original method or store credit, restock items, notify the customer.

gap: Refund, restock, partial refund, cancel and customer email work (order-admin.int.test.ts); no refund as store credit.
criteria: Staff refund any amount up to what is left through Stripe on the store's account, with Kaizen's fee on that part returned (`refund_application_fee`); more than is left is refused.
Chosen items go back in stock, with or without money back; only physical lines, and never more than were bought.
Cancelling a paid, unsent order refunds everything left, restocks and closes it; a sent order cannot be cancelled.
The customer is emailed once per refund; returns and withdrawals refund through the same path (D153).
Staff can refund to a store credit balance the shopper can use at checkout, recorded in an append-only ledger (integration test, euro scenario).

history.why: Shopify refunds to store credit; Kaizen refunds to the original method only
